Expectation1: Ensure client satisfaction and address any concerns or complaints professionally
Situation1: An easygoing regular politely asks for a tiny adjustment to their fringe.
Expectation2: Raise public awareness about social inequities and marginalized groups
Situation2: They respond to an urgent incident of discrimination that requires immediate public attention and awareness.
Story: I was halfway through trimming Maria’s fringe, her laughter filling the salon as she recounted her weekend, when she glanced in the mirror and hesitated. “Could you just take a little more off here?” she asked, touching her brow. I smiled, ready to oblige—client satisfaction was everything, especially with regulars like Maria. But as I reached for my scissors, my phone buzzed insistently in my pocket. A message from the advocacy group flashed on the screen: “Urgent—discrimination incident at City Hall. Need you to go live now.” My heart pounded. I was the designated spokesperson today, expected to raise awareness and rally support in real time. Maria’s trust in my work tugged at me, but so did the voices of those who needed me to speak up. I felt the weight of both worlds pressing in, my hands trembling as I tried to steady the comb, torn between the quiet needs of one and the urgent cries of many.
